claims.paper_title: Lipid nanoparticles for mRNA delivery
claims.text: The ionizable lipid is the key determinant of potency, facilitating mRNA encapsulation and endosomal escape.

claims.paper_title: Lipid nanoparticles for mRNA delivery
claims.text: Here, we review the design principles of LNPs, their structure-activity relationships, and emerging strategies for tissue-specific delivery.

claims.paper_title: Lipid nanoparticles for mRNA delivery
claims.text: We identify several key gaps: the exact mechanism of endosomal escape remains controversial, extrahepatic targeting strategies have limited success in vivo, and the relationship between lipid pKa and in vivo efficacy is incompletely understood.

claims.paper_title: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles for RNA delivery: design, mechanism, and applications
claims.text: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles for RNA delivery: design, mechanism, and applications  Ionizable lipids are the central functional component of lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) for RNA delivery.

claims.paper_title: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles for RNA delivery: design, mechanism, and applications
claims.text: Key structure-activity relationships include the influence of tail length, unsaturation, and headgroup pKa on delivery efficiency.

claims.paper_title: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles for RNA delivery: design, mechanism, and applications
claims.text: The pKa of ionizable lipids correlates with in vivo potency, with an optimal pKa around 6.2-6.5 for hepatocyte delivery.

claims.paper_title: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles for RNA delivery: design, mechanism, and applications
claims.text: However, mechanistic understanding of how ionizable lipids facilitate endosomal escape is still evolving.

claims.paper_title: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles for RNA delivery: design, mechanism, and applications
claims.text: Current evidence suggests that ionizable lipids disrupt the endosomal membrane through a flip-flop mechanism involving protonation-deprotonation cycles, but direct experimental evidence for this model remains limited.

claims.paper_title: Combinatorial design of ionizable lipids for lipid nanoparticle delivery of mRNA
claims.text: However, translation to extrahepatic tissues was not achieved, and the precise relationship between lipid structure and intracellular trafficking remains poorly understood.

claims.paper_title: Endosomal escape of lipid nanoparticles: a mechanistic investigation
claims.text: Endosomal escape of lipid nanoparticles: a mechanistic investigation  The mechanism by which lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) escape the endosome is not fully understood.

claims.paper_title: Endosomal escape of lipid nanoparticles: a mechanistic investigation
claims.text: We found that less than 5% of internalized mRNA reached the cytosol, indicating that endosomal escape is a major bottleneck.

claims.paper_title: Endosomal escape of lipid nanoparticles: a mechanistic investigation
claims.text: Ionizable lipids promoted membrane destabilization through a pH-dependent phase transition from lamellar to inverted hexagonal structures.

claims.paper_title: Endosomal escape of lipid nanoparticles: a mechanistic investigation
claims.text: These findings suggest that endosomal escape efficiency must be improved at least 10-fold for LNP-based therapeutics to achieve their full potential.

claims.paper_title: Extrahepatic targeting of lipid nanoparticles in vivo
claims.text: A major barrier is the rapid formation of a protein corona on LNPs after injection, which masks targeting ligands and redirects particles to the liver.

claims.paper_title: CRISPR-Cas9 lipid nanoparticle systems for in vivo gene editing
claims.text: High-performance LNPs with optimized ionizable lipid MC3 achieved the highest editing in hepatocytes, but extrahepatic editing remains elusive.

claims.paper_title: Structure-activity relationships of ionizable lipids for lipid nanoparticle delivery
claims.text: Structure-activity relationships of ionizable lipids for lipid nanoparticle delivery  We synthesized and evaluated 100+ ionizable lipidoids to understand structure-activity relationships (SAR) for mRNA delivery.

claims.paper_title: Structure-activity relationships of ionizable lipids for lipid nanoparticle delivery
claims.text: Key findings: (1) lipid pKa between 6.0-6.8 is critical for in vivo potency, (2) unsaturated tails (C18:1, C18:2) outperform saturated tails, (3) ester linkages improve biodegradability without sacrificing activity, (4) tail length of C12-C16 provides optimal delivery.

claims.paper_title: Structure-activity relationships of ionizable lipids for lipid nanoparticle delivery
claims.text: However, the same SAR rules do not apply across different administration routes (IV vs IM vs SC).

claims.paper_title: Structure-activity relationships of ionizable lipids for lipid nanoparticle delivery
claims.text: Important gaps remain: the role of lipid shape in membrane curvature induction during endosomal escape is poorly characterized, and most SAR studies have been limited to a small number of cell types.

claims.paper_title: Biodistribution and pharmacokinetics of lipid nanoparticle-formulated mRNA
claims.text: Surprisingly, despite rapid hepatic uptake, only 2-5% of internalized mRNA was translated into protein, suggesting that LNP unpackaging and endosomal escape within hepatocytes is inefficient.

claims.paper_title: Small interfering RNA delivery via lipid nanoparticles for liver target engagement
claims.text: Despite this success, several challenges remain: (1) extrahepatic delivery has not been clinically achieved, (2) LNP-mediated siRNA delivery requires relatively high doses (0.3 mg/kg), (3) the mechanism of intracellular release remains incompletely understood, and (4) immunogenicity limits repeat dosing.

claims.paper_title: mRNA vaccines against COVID-19: a perspective on LNP formulation design
claims.text: Key gaps include: (1) mechanisms of LNP-induced inflammation remain poorly understood, (2) the contribution of specific lipid components to immune activation versus delivery efficiency is unclear, and (3) developing thermostable formulations that eliminate cold chain requirements remains a significant engineering challenge.

claims.paper_title: Nucleoside-modified mRNA-LNP therapeutics beyond vaccines: protein replacement and gene editing
claims.text: Current LNPs are also less efficient at transducing primary cells compared to established cell lines, and the relationship between LNP composition and protein corona formation in different disease states is not understood.

claims.paper_title: Advances in lipid nanoparticle delivery of nucleic acids and beyond
claims.text: We examine current understanding of LNP-cell interactions: cellular uptake (clathrin- and caveolae-mediated endocytosis), endosomal trafficking, and the poorly characterized mechanism of endosomal escape.

claims.paper_title: Lipid nanoparticle chemistry: from RNA delivery to the next generation of therapeutics
claims.text: Despite extensive SAR studies, fundamental questions remain: the precise molecular requirements for efficient endosomal escape are unknown, the role of lipid metabolism in nanoparticle clearance is underexplored, and predictive models for immunogenicity based on lipid structure have not been developed.

claims.paper_title: The endosomal escape of lipid nanoparticles: mechanisms and strategies for improvement
claims.text: The endosomal escape of lipid nanoparticles: mechanisms and strategies for improvement  Endosomal escape is the most critical bottleneck for lipid nanoparticle (LNP)-mediated nucleic acid delivery.

claims.paper_title: The endosomal escape of lipid nanoparticles: mechanisms and strategies for improvement
claims.text: However, improvements in endosomal escape often correlate with increased toxicity, suggesting that potent escape and biocompatibility may require decoupling through novel chemical approaches.

topics.title: Decoupling innate immune activation from LNP delivery potency
topics.hypothesis: Ionizable lipid structure independently drives TLR/inflammasome activation versus endosomal escape; lipids can be optimized for high delivery with low reactogenicity.
proposed_experiments: Screen ionizable lipids for IL-6/IFN reporter activation in vitro
Correlate innate activation with endosomal escape efficiency
Validate low-inflammation high-potency candidates in mice
topics.expected_readout: ≥2× potency/inflammation ratio vs SM-102 or MC3 reference LNPs.
topics.feasibility_notes: Cell reporter assays are accessible; in vivo cytokine panels standard.
topics.impact_rationale: Addresses 3 scored gaps in 'immunogenicity' (cluster mean overall=0.70). Success would advance therapeutically relevant nucleic acid delivery.

topics.title: Ligand-displaying LNPs for extrahepatic targeting: avidity vs specificity
topics.hypothesis: Multivalent display of low-affinity targeting ligands (e.g., mannose, transferrin, or anti-CD3 scFv) on LNP surfaces achieves higher tissue selectivity than high-affinity monovalent targeting, due to reduced off-target uptake by liver macrophages.
proposed_experiments: Synthesize LNPs with controlled densities of selected ligands (0–100% surface coverage)
Quantify uptake in target vs off-target cells with flow cytometry
Test in vivo biodistribution with reporter mRNAs in xenograft or disease models
topics.expected_readout: Target-to-liver uptake ratio; ≥5× improvement over non-targeted LNPs.
topics.feasibility_notes: Lipid-PEG-ligand chemistry is standard; main risk is synthesis scale-up.
topics.impact_rationale: Addresses 3 scored gaps in 'targeting' (cluster mean overall=0.67). Success would advance therapeutically relevant nucleic acid delivery.

topics.title: Pharmacokinetic determinants of repeat-dose LNP nucleic acid delivery
topics.hypothesis: PEG-lipid desorption kinetics and anti-PEG IgM jointly dominate accelerated blood clearance on redosing; tunable PEG-lipid anchors can restore multi-dose exposure.
proposed_experiments: Vary PEG-lipid anchor length and measure circulation half-life over 3 weekly doses
Quantify anti-PEG antibodies and correlate with clearance
Test alternative stealth polymers (e.g., polysarcosine) as PEG replacements
topics.expected_readout: Dose 3 exposure ≥70% of dose 1 AUC for lead formulation.
topics.feasibility_notes: Standard PK study design; antibody assays commercially available.
topics.impact_rationale: Addresses 2 scored gaps in 'pks' (cluster mean overall=0.65). Success would advance therapeutically relevant nucleic acid delivery.

topics.title: Mechanistic understanding of LNP endosomal escape: fusion vs destabilization
topics.hypothesis: Endosomal escape of LNPs proceeds primarily through membrane destabilization (ionizable lipid-facilitated flip-flop and bilayer disruption) rather than fusogenic mechanisms, and can be enhanced by helper lipids that lower the lamellar-to-hexagonal phase transition temperature.
proposed_experiments: Labelled lipid mixing vs content release assays to distinguish fusion from destabilization
Cryo-ET of LNPs in endosomal compartments at timed intervals after uptake
Vary helper lipid ratios and correlate with endosomal escape efficiency via FRET
topics.expected_readout: Quantitative fraction of delivered cargo reaching cytosol vs lysosomal degradation.
topics.feasibility_notes: Requires advanced microscopy (cryo-ET) — moderate; FRET assays are accessible.
topics.impact_rationale: Addresses 3 scored gaps in 'endosomal_escape' (cluster mean overall=0.64). Success would advance therapeutically relevant nucleic acid delivery.

topics.title: Quantitative bottleneck analysis of the LNP delivery cascade
topics.hypothesis: Endosomal escape—not uptake or encapsulation—is the dominant loss term in the delivery cascade for most clinical-like LNP compositions, and 10× escape gains are necessary and sufficient for transformative dose reduction.
proposed_experiments: Build a quantitative cascade map (injection→uptake→escape→translation) with barcoded mRNA
Perturb each step independently and measure sensitivity of protein output
Identify the step with highest elasticity for dose reduction
topics.expected_readout: Ranked elasticities per cascade step; validated 5× dose reduction via top lever.
topics.feasibility_notes: Requires careful assay development; high scientific payoff.
topics.impact_rationale: Addresses 2 scored gaps in 'delivery_efficiency' (cluster mean overall=0.64). Success would advance therapeutically relevant nucleic acid delivery.

timeline.label: Kickoff
timeline.title: Scope with Asst Prof Smargon
timeline.body: Not generic lit-search. Theory↔experiment gaps; LLM memorization safeguards; NA chemistry/delivery domain. Early progress welcome before formal August start.

timeline.label: Iteration 1
timeline.title: Working vertical slice + private multi-page board
timeline.body: End-to-end agent shipped. LLM run 15 papers → 91 claims, 102 evidence, 47 gaps, 5 topics. Living board for async updates.

timeline.label: Planned
timeline.title: Formal start + Stage 2
timeline.body: BG4801 when eligible. Embeddings, memorization bench, larger corpus, optional second domain. Updates continue on this board.

timeline.label: Cadence
timeline.title: Async progress updates
timeline.body: Each iteration adds a timeline entry and refreshed metrics so progress is reviewable without a formal meeting.
